transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-20
Time: 15:00 - 15:42 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Lina Martinez (Redwood AE), Devon Chang (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM); Karen O'Neill (Aurora Procurement), Rahul Verma (Aurora Legal), Tara Singh (Aurora Security), Matt Holt (Aurora Engineering)

Auto-generated Summary:
- Procurement/legal review of MSA and DPA; customer requested clarifications on data residency, encryption/KMS clauses, and audit log retention.
- SLA discussion: Aurora wants a 99.9% uptime SLA for critical routes and stronger incident response timelines. Redwood proposed tiered SLA with credits and dedicated option.
- Pricing/commits: Reviewed reserved capacity and burst options; customer asked for pilot pricing metric and month-to-month transition to committed capacity.
- Next steps: Redwood to send updated redline, SE to run latency benchmark, legal teams to align on DPA edits.

Topics:
- MSA terms and liabilities
- DPA data processing and KMS
- SLA targets and credits
- Onboarding and pilot pricing

Transcript:
[00:00] Lina: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check on audio, can you all hear me?
[00:06] Karen: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:08] Rahul: Yes, hi.
[00:10] Lina: Great. Goal for today is to run through the MSA/DPA redlines and SLA items so legal and procurement can call out any blockers. Devon and Priya are here to cover technical / onboarding.
[00:22] Devon: Hi all. I'll jump into the SLA and technical aspects when we hit those slides.
[00:27] Matt: Quick note from engineering — we did a spike on connecting our VPC via the private peering flow, so we'll want to confirm Redwood's VPC egress IP ranges for firewall rules.
[00:36] Devon: Yep, we'll share the IP ranges. There's also an option for customer-managed deployment but it adds ops overhead.
[00:44] Tara: On security, the big asks are KMS integration (HSM optional), audit logs retention for 7 years, and attestations for SOC2 plus an ISO inquiry.
[00:57] Priya: We can share SOC2 cert and the console compliance guide, that's standard.
[01:02] Rahul: On the DPA, section 4.2 around subprocessors — we need a clearer notification window and right to object. Current wording seems open-ended.
[01:12] Lina: Understood. Our legal team usually does a 30-day notice for new subprocessors and a right-to-object process, but we can make that explicit in the DPA.
[01:20] Karen: Also liability caps in the MSA: Aurora's counsel is asking for explicit carveouts for data breaches caused by Redwood's negligence, and a higher cap for security incidents.
[01:32] Lina: We typically have a liability cap tied to 12 months of fees, with exclusion for gross negligence and willful misconduct. We can talk specifics — are you looking for a higher multiple?
[01:40] Rahul: We'd prefer 24 months for security-related incidents, given the sensitivity of finance data.
[01:46] Lina: Okay, that's a negotiation point but we can propose a 24-month cap for security incidents; need to confirm with finance.
[01:52] Matt: From an engineering perspective, we care less about the cap and more about incident response SLAs and forensic support. We need 24/7 incident response contact and 2-hour initial acknowledgement for Sev 1.
[02:05] Devon: Our dedicated customers can get 2-hour ack; hosted plan has longer ack. We can map to dedicated or premium SLA.
[02:12] Tara: Can you confirm what logs are available via the console and what we can export? We need immutable audit logs and a way to push to our SIEM.
[02:20] Priya: We have streaming audit logs to customer Kinesis/Splunk and export APIs. We'll send the export spec after the call.
[02:28] Karen: About data residency — Aurora has EU and US tenants; we need guaranteed region pinning for EU data. Does Redwood offer regional pinning and data residency guarantees?
[02:38] Lina: Yes, we offer region pinning for both hosted and dedicated. For hosted, we can pin workloads to eu-west and us-east regions; dedicated gives stronger guarantees and isolation.
[02:47] Rahul: We need the contract to state data won't be transferred outside designated region without consent.
[02:52] Lina: That's reasonable; we'll add a clause to the DPA that prohibits cross-region transfer without written consent.
[02:58] Matt: On onboarding timing — if we start a pilot, what's the expected timeline to production? We're aiming for 8 weeks post-signing.
[03:07] Devon: Typical pilot is 2–4 weeks for evaluation and 4–6 for integration depending on complexity. For a dedicated profile it may take longer for capacity provisioning.
[03:18] Karen: Pricing — procurement asked for a pilot discount and a path to committed pricing after 90 days. Any flexibility there?
[03:25] Lina: We can offer pilot pricing credits and then a committed discount moving to reserved capacity with monthly billing. I'll include options in the pricing sheet.
[03:34] Rahul: A few specific DPA items — deletion vs retention: Aurora wants a documented data deletion SLA after contract termination and a certification of deletion.
[03:44] Priya: We provide deletion certificates for Customer data and retention of logs per agreed period.
[03:49] Tara: About encryption — we insist on customer-managed keys for production PII; is that supported?
[03:54] Devon: Yes, KMS integration with customer keys (bring your own key) is supported on dedicated and private deployments; hosted supports CMEK for select tiers.
[04:03] Karen: Can you confirm backup retention? We need backups encrypted and retained per the retention schedule, with clear restore procedures.
[04:11] Devon: Backups are encrypted at rest and in transit; retention is configurable — we'll include recommended retention settings in the onboarding doc.
[04:20] Rahul: On indemnities: we want clearer IP indemnity for model outputs that might contain third-party copyrighted text. Current MSA section is vague.
[04:30] Lina: Fair point. We have model usage language that limits liability for model outputs, but for enterprise customers we can add stronger indemnity language subject to review.
[04:38] Karen: What about cryptic stuff — like continuous learning and model training? We won't allow customer data to be used to improve public models.
[04:45] Priya: By default, customer data isn't used for model training; we'll make that explicit in the DPA.
[04:50] Rahul: Good. Also want a maximum time for Redwood to notify us of a security breach — 72 hours is typical; will Redwood commit to that?
[04:58] Lina: We commit to 72-hour notification for confirmed breaches, and earlier if possible. We'll add that.
[05:05] Matt: Infra question — if we need private deployment on-prem, what's the rough lead time and support level?
[05:12] Devon: On-prem is longer: typically 8–12 weeks plus integration. We offer an ops package for on-prem customers.
[05:18] Karen: One last commercial point — need to confirm payment terms, tax treatment, and whether Redwood accepts ACH and wire.
[05:26] Lina: Standard is net 30; we support ACH/wire and will note tax handling per region in the quote.
[05:33] Rahul: Ok I think we have the list of redlines, I'll consolidate with procurement.
[05:38] Lina: Great. We'll plan to send a redlined MSA/DPA with proposed language and a pricing addendum by Friday.
[05:46] Karen: Perfect.
[05:49] -- Later in call, deep-dive onto SLA specifics --
[20:00] Devon: For SLA we propose: 99.9% uptime for API endpoints for dedicated customers, 99.5% for hosted; incident ack times 2 hours for Sev1 on dedicated, 4 hours on hosted, remediation timelines depend on severity. Credits are prorated by downtime minutes.
[20:20] Matt: Need the math on credits and whether credits cap at fees; also ask for SLA reporting access.
[20:28] Priya: We'll give route-level dashboards and monthly SLA reports.
[20:34] Rahul: Also want a termination right if SLA is repeatedly missed — like two consecutive months below threshold triggers termination.
[20:42] Lina: We can include termination right for repeated breaches, subject to a cure period.
[20:48] Karen: On insurance and risk, Aurora requires proof of cyber insurance with minimum coverage. Can you provide certificate?
[20:56] Lina: Yes, we'll provide the COI and policy summary to procurement.
[21:02] -- Closing minutes --
[38:30] Lina: Recap: Redwood will send updated MSA/DPA with explicit subprocessors notice, data residency clause, 72-hour breach notif, CMEK language, and a proposed 24-month cap for security incidents (to be confirmed). SE will run benchmark and share IP ranges and export spec. Pricing and pilot terms will be included.
[38:55] Karen: We'll aim to have consolidated redlines and procurement feedback by next Tuesday.
[39:05] Rahul: Legal will review and send questions within the week.
[39:12] Matt: Engineering will test the peering once we get IP ranges.
[39:19] Priya: I'll also schedule onboarding kickoff contingent on signed DPA.
[39:25] Lina: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the doc package.
[39:30] Karen: Thanks all.
[39:33] -- call ends --

Notes about transcript: transcription contains occasional name misspellings (e.g., KMS sometimes transcribed as K M S), and some overlap in speaker labels. The content above was lightly edited for readability but preserves filler and interruptions typical of sales calls.
